newsitem.title: USA: Attorneys say alleged Miami hijacker feared Cuba life.
newsitem.headline: Attorneys say alleged Miami hijacker feared Cuba life.

text.p: A Palestinian man charged with hijacking a Havana-bound Spanish airliner to Miami last summer did so because he did not want to go to Cuba where he had been sent by an anti-Israeli group for military training, his attorney said on Tuesday.

Saad'o Mohamed Ibrahim Intissar, who was born and raised in a Lebanese refugee camp, faces air piracy charges for allegedly using a fake bomb and a makeshift knife to divert Iberia Flight 6621 and force it to land in Miami on July 26. The jet was carrying 231 passengers and crew.

"He did not threaten to hurt anyone else...," said public defender Joaquin Mendez, Intissar's attorney. "He pointed it at himself and said that he would rather die and that he would kill himself rather than go to Havana."

During the prosecution's opening argument, Assistant U.S. Attorney Daryl Trawick spelled out how Intissar, who was taken into custody immediately after the DC-10 landed in Miami, burst into the plane's cockpit about six hours after it left Madrid and demanded that it not complete its trip to Havana.
"The defendant... is guilty of the crime of air piracy," he said.
Mendez agreed that Intissar burst into the cockpit and said he had a bomb. "We're not here to argue too much about what he did, we are here to argue about why he did what he did," he said.

Mendez described how Intissar had worked as a bodyguard for groups that recruit Palestinians from refugee camps in Lebanon and that he was sent to Cuba by an organisation called the Islamic Revolutionary Army, which Mendez said was connected to the Iranian-supported Hezbollah organisation.
Mendez said Intissar tried to avoid the trip first by destroying his travel documents, and then by seeking to escape from airports in Beirut, Zurich and Madrid during his trip.

Mendez stressed that Intissar agreed to surrender peacefully as soon as he was told the jet would not go to Cuba. "He is grateful for the opportunity to land in the United States and to seek political asylum," he said.
U.S. District Judge Lenore Nesbitt said if convicted Intissar faced a minimum mandatory sentence of 20 years in prison. Intissar has pleaded not guilty to air piracy,
A panel of 12 jurors and two alternates was selected earlier Tuesday.
